session_summary: Sprint: render altered ferry schedule during disruptions. Shipped end-to-end: backend parseTimesFromMessage() extracts HH:MM departure times from the City of Toronto's free-text disruption messages; hook separates City closed (→ 'suspended') from alert (→ 'disrupted'); frontend renders departure chips during disruptions instead of just the error message; Billy Bishop Airport added to sidebar schedule; 11 new unit tests. 5 beads closed (601, 46u, rth, 3ao, 8sz). PR #13 opened. bd stats: 40/40 closed, 0 open, 0 blocked.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Reliable on Task 4a (5 min, 30 turns clean) when given precise pre-computed anchors and replacement code blocks.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Task 3 (hook + test fixtures) hit max_turns=20 with 4 residual TS errors because the test file had its own duplicate buildRouteStatuses + multiple fixture literals to update.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: When dispatching tasks that touch both production code AND parallel test fixtures, surface the test file as a separately-budgeted concern in the task description, or split production+test edits across two tasks.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Wrote tests, ran all gates, made the commit, and named the branch correctly — the productive part of the task ran clean.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Hit max_turns=35 at the final 'open PR' step. Producing the gh pr create HEREDOC body from scratch was expensive in turns.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Either bump default qa-tester max_turns to 45 when a PR step is included, or delegate the PR-open step to pr-opener as a follow-up. Consider giving qa-tester a built-in PR template helper.

agent_feedback.worked_well: N/A — failed at max_turns=8 even for a trivial git push + gh pr create.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Cold-start cost + processing the HEREDOC PR body in the prompt consumed the entire budget before any tool call landed.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Either raise pr-opener default max_turns to 12 OR change its template to expect the PR title/body to be pre-rendered into a file the agent just reads + passes through. Right now any task with a non-trivial body is a coin flip.

overall_notes: Voltron mid-session updates v3.2.0 → v3.3.2 → v3.3.3 were seamless once stale containers (from before the update) were stopped. The new polling cadence in v3.3.x scrum-master template eliminated the wait-and-poll guesswork from earlier. Auto-updated agent .md files appeared as unstaged changes — was careful to exclude them from the feature commit. Tools touched: bd, gh, docker, npm, vitest. Pattern observed: orchestrator handling git push + gh pr create directly is consistently faster than dispatching a Docker agent for the same trivial operation (cold-start dominates).
